title: Master in Oncology, Translational Immunology and Aging

breadcrumb.label: Master in Oncology, Translational Immunology and Aging

blocks.html:
The Master of Science in Oncology, Translational Immunology and Aging (MOTIA) is an advanced, research-oriented graduate programme offered by the Faculty of Biomedical Sciences at Università della Svizzera italiana (USI). The programme is deeply rooted in the Bios⁺ research ecosystem in Bellinzona, which hosts the Institute for Research in Biomedicine (IRB) and the Institute of Oncology Research (IOR), leading institutes affiliated with USI, as well as the Institute for Translational Research USI-EOC (IRT), ensuring direct exposure to pioneering biomedical research and real-world scientific challenges.

MOTIA provides a solid foundation in the core principles of oncology, immunology, and aging biology, combined with rigorous training in translational research approaches that bridge basic science and clinical application. Students will learn to integrate cutting-edge scientific knowledge with experimental and analytical skills, advancing from fundamental mechanisms of disease to innovative strategies for diagnosis, prevention, and therapy.

The Master, which is taught entirely in English, strongly emphasises hands-on learning through laboratory immersion and research practice. Students are embedded in a research group from an early stage through the First Lab Experience module, and progressively develop independent research skills, culminating in a 60 ECTS Master's thesis conducted over the second year.

items.title: Who we are
items.html:
MOTIA’s scientific committee comprises six leading researchers, who carry out their research at the Bios⁺ research ecosystem.

Greta Guarda

Greta Guarda

Full Professor, Faculty of Biomedical Sciences

Greta Guarda studied in Zurich, established her independent research group in immunology in Lausanne in 2012, and moved to the IRB in 2018. She has taught immunology at the University of Lausanne and the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology in Zurich.

Read

Lucio Barile

Lucio Barile

Adjunct Professor, Faculty of Biomedical Sciences

Lucio Barile received his academic training at the University of Rome “La Sapienza,” where he earned a Master’s degree in Pharmacy and a PhD in Experimental Medicine, and further developed his expertise in cardiovascular research through research experiences at Johns Hopkins University in Baltimore, the ICGEB in Trieste, and the University of Milano-Bicocca.

For more information about his project see: www.irt.usi-eoc.ch/cardiology.

Read

Arianna Calcinotto

Arianna Calcinotto

Assistant Professor, Faculty of Biomedical Sciences

Arianna Calcinotto trained in molecular medicine and cancer immunology in Milan, at the Mayo Clinic in the US, and at the Institute of Oncology Research (IOR) in Bellinzona, where she established her independent research group in 2019 (https://ior.usi.ch/team-cancer-immunotherapy-lab). She is an Assistant Professor at the Università della Svizzera italiana (USI) and teaches cancer immunotherapy at ETH Zurich.

Read

Petr Cejka

Petr Cejka

Full Professor, Faculty of Biomedical Sciences

Petr Cejka trained in molecular biology, DNA repair and protein biochemistry at Charles University in Prague, the University of Zurich, and the University of California, Davis. He established his independent research group at the University of Zurich in 2011 and moved to the Institute for Research in Biomedicine (IRB) in Bellinzona in 2016, where he leads the Recombination Mechanisms laboratory. He is a Full Professor at the Università della Svizzera italiana (USI) and an EMBO member.

Read

Giandomenica Iezzi

Giandomenica Iezzi

Adjunct professor, Faculty of Biomedical Sciences

Giandomenica Iezzi trained in medicine at the University of Milan, where she earned an MD degree and a specialization in Immunology and Clinical Allergology. She further developed her expertise in cancer immunology through research experiences at the San Raffaele Hospital in Milan, the Basel Institute for Immunology, ETH Zurich, and the Department of Biomedicine at the University of Basel, where she established her independent research group. In 2019, she moved to the Ente Ospedaliero Cantonale (EOC) in Bellinzona. For more information see this link.

Read

Vittorio Limongelli

Vittorio Limongelli

Full Professor, Faculty of Biomedical Sciences

Professor Limongelli earned his PhD in Drug Sciences and completed his postdoctoral training at ETH Zurich, where he specialized in computational approaches to drug discovery. He has received several international awards in medicinal and computational chemistry, including an ERC Consolidator Grant in 2020. He is the author of more than 70 publications in leading scientific journals.

items.title: The three Institutes
items.html:
Institute of Oncology Research (IOR)

The Institute of Oncology Research hosts researchers from all over the world performing basic, translational, and applied research in oncology with special focus on cancer biology, genomics, molecular oncology, and experimental therapeutics

Learn more about IOR: https://ior.usi.ch/.

Institute for Research in Biomedicine (IRB)

The Institute for Research in Biomedicine was founded in 2000 with the goal of advancing the study of human immunology, with particular emphasis on the mechanisms of host defense. The activities of the 13 research groups now extend beyond immunology to include the fields of DNA repair, rare diseases, structural and cell biology.

Learn more about IRB: https://irb.usi.ch/.

Institute for Translational Research (IRT)

The Institute for Translational Research is dedicated to applied biomedical research through a multidisciplinary approach, aimed at improving health and deepening the understanding of human disease.

Learn more about IRT: www.irt.usi-eoc.ch.

items.title: Are the degrees issued by USI recognised internationally?
items.html:
Università della Svizzera italiana (USI) is a recognised or accredited Swiss university. Academic qualifications obtained at USI Faculties are therefore also recognised abroad, on the basis of international conventions.

  1. The mutual recognition of academic qualifications, i.e. the diplomas awarded by universities and universities of applied sciences, that enables students to continue with their studies is governed by the Lisbon Convention of 11 April 1997 and other international conventions with Germany, Italy, Austria and France.
    With regard to relations with ITALY, in particular:
    Accordo tra il Governo della Repubblica Italiana ed il Consiglio Federale Svizzero sul reciproco riconoscimento delle equivalenze nel settore universitario. (Agreement between the Government the Italian Republic and the Swiss Federal Council on the mutual recognition of academic qualifications)
    The agreement establishes the principle of equal treatment of Italian and Swiss students. Mutual recognition applies to university degrees and diplomas, exam performance and the equivalence of study periods, taking into account the ECTS credits system. Degrees awarded by a university that authorises the holder to continue his/her studies or to undertake the next course of studies at a university in one of the two Contracting States, without additional examinations, shall confer the same right in the other Contracting State.
    In addition, the holder of a degree awarded by a university in one of the two Contracting States shall be entitled to make use of that degree in the other State in the form provided for by the legislation of the State in which it was awarded.
    Professional rights shall not be directly linked to the right to make use of a university degree.
  2. The recognition of the professional qualifications of Swiss and EU/EFTA nationals wishing to pursue a regulated profession is governed by the Agreement on the free movement of persons and the EFTA Convention.
    With regard to accessing professional practice in Italy for those who have obtained their university degree at USI, paragraph 1 letter d) of Presidential Decree 189/2009 applies, according to which it is required to submit the documents indicated in the Presidential Decree to the professional association, which, in turn, transmits them to the MIUR (Ministero dell'Università e della Ricerca) which recognizes the validity of the foreign qualification for access to professional practice.

Useful links:
Procedures for the recognition of foreign qualifications in Italy (http://www.cimea.it/en)
Procedures for the certification of the authenticity of USI diplomas (In Italian only) (https://www4.ti.ch/decs/dcsu/ucsu)
Information on the recognition of foreign qualifications and competent recognition authorities in Switzerland (https://www.sbfi.admin.ch/sbfi/en/home/education/recognition-of-foreign-qualifications/recognition-procedure-on-establishment/agencies-responsible-for-the-recognition-of-foreign-qualificatio.html)
